title: LSP: on_new_config for vim.lsp.config
body:
### Problem

nvim-lspconfig has a `on_new_config` feature which is apparently not addressed by vim.lsp.config. The documentation for `on_new_config` is:

> Function executed after a root directory is detected. Used to modify the server configuration (including `cmd` itself).


### Expected behavior

ref https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig/pull/3597#issuecomment-2628425734

> This could be another application for an autocmd that triggers just before the client starts. Or maybe could just be done in RTP.

Edit: maybe `root_dir()` is already flexible enough?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: The main requirement I gathered from that issue is that windows executables need to be mapped to another name. Arguably I think this should just be done in the config directly rather than using some hook to achieve it later on in the flow.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Yeah. For reference, see https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig/pull/3592#issuecomment-2619481770 for the apparent motivation for that Angular `on_new_config` handler (seems like something the LSP server should do...).

I'd prefer that we avoid `on_new_config` (as a concept), but opened this to gather feedback on whether it is needed.

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
I use it to load project specific configuration for LSPs that don't have their own configuration files.

Something like this 
```lua
local function load_config(root_dir)
    local path = Path:new(root_dir, ".nvimlsp")
    if path:exists() then
        path = tostring(path)
        local config = {}
        local f, err = loadfile(path, "bt", config)
        if f ~= nil then
            f()
            return config
        else
            print(err)
        end
    end
    return nil
end

local function on_new_config(new_config, new_root_dir)
    local project_options = load_config(new_root_dir)
    if project_options then
        local serveropts = project_options[new_config.name]
        if serveropts ~= nil then
            local new = vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", new_config, serveropts)
            for k, v in pairs(new) do
                new_config[k] = v
            end
        end
    end
end
```

`exrc`, does not quite cut it for me since I usually have one nvim instance, with multiple projects open, one project per tab, with `:<nick>` selecting the working directory. And I also often switch projects on the fly.

comments.author: participant5
comments.body:
Don't mean to add any unnecessary noise, but as someone who does use `on_new_config` pretty regularly, I figured it would be useful to share the main pattern all of my uses seem to follow. All of the cases where I have used `on_new_config` seem to be dynamically building the command used to execute the language server. This is useful in a few places specifically:

- Dynamically building the command line arguments passed to start the server
  - some language servers use command line flags to pass in configuration files if they aren't super good at following the configuration options in the LSP spec
  - cases where java is used to execute the language server there are a ton of flags for the jvm runtime that can be built dynamically to properly link libraries/configure memory requirements/etc.
- Some languages with virtual environments you may want to detect in some way if there is a different location for the command binary and fill that in accordingly

Not that this is necessarily an argument for or against `on_new_config`, there could be a better formalization that also covers cases like these

reporter
comments.body:
# Resolution

AFAICT, all the above use-cases are already addressed:

> other use cases ... to determine if a language server supports multiple workspaces to trigger didChangeConfiguration and also remember context about the new workspace folders seen

Isn't that the use-case for [dynamic root_dir()](https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/33446#discussion_r2062720286) (which is already supported)?

> Dynamically building the command line arguments passed to start the server

`cmd` can be a function. However, we don't provide an example, and it's probably not as convenient as the `cmd:string[]` form. https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/52a4bc45488cb1f626b02be5512cd0301cd48cb8/runtime/doc/lsp.txt#L1306-L1307

> languages with virtual environments you may want to detect in some way if there is a different location for the command binary

`cmd` can be a function.

> see [neovim/nvim-lspconfig#3592 (comment)](https://github.com/neovim/nvim-lspconfig/pull/3592#issuecomment-2619481770) for the apparent motivation for that Angular `on_new_config` handler

`cmd` can be a function.

> I use it to load project specific configuration for LSPs that don't have their own configuration files.

Did you try `reuse_client:fun()` ? https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/07a207a5f16be98053a56cc0a20d182717deaf54/runtime/doc/lsp.txt#L711-L715

Other ideas:

- a `FileType` event handler can`vim.lsp.config('foo')` modify the config. 
- `:<nick> 'exrc'` now mentions:
  ```
    To achieve project-local LSP configuration:
    1. Enable 'exrc'.
    2. Place LSP configs at ".nvim/lsp/*.lua" in your project root.
    3. Create ".nvim.lua" in your project root directory with this line: >lua
         vim.cmd[[set runtimepath+=.nvim]]
  ```


> The ccls language server can only be configured through `init_options`, so making changes in `on_attach` is to late

Did you try `before_init` ?  https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/52a4bc45488cb1f626b02be5512cd0301cd48cb8/runtime/doc/lsp.txt#L1388-L1389

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
A bit late, but I think I have a use case that is not covered without `on_new_config` (correct me I'm wrong, I'd be happy to be wrong here).

I have a plugin that I've been working on for a while now: [devcontainers.nvim](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim). I've been using it for quite some time and it's working for me without any issues. The plugin allows to spawn LSP server inside a devcontainer while Neovim is running on the host (outside of container). It then wraps `config.cmd` by ([using its function form with RPC dispatchers](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim/blob/112f52fe966c795c6a095bc83b743dcfc5e56fcb/lua/devcontainers/lsp/rpc.lua#L275)) and performs URI path mapping between host and container in LSP messages. It uses LSP [metaModel.json](https://microsoft.github.io/language-server-protocol/specifications/lsp/3.17/specification/#metaModel) (provided along LSP specification) to find all message types that container URIs and to find all places ("paths") in messages where URI can exist, this way it can efficiently and reliably translate the URIs. This is also described [here](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim?tab=readme-ov-file#-design).

Now, I use `on_new_config` for multiple things, [here is the on_new_config implementation](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim/blob/112f52fe966c795c6a095bc83b743dcfc5e56fcb/lua/devcontainers/init.lua#L17). The most important "feature" of `on_new_config` is that it is running in a Lua coroutine. This way my plugin can check if the devcontainer is already running and [spawn it](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim/blob/112f52fe966c795c6a095bc83b743dcfc5e56fcb/lua/devcontainers/init.lua#L40) if needed. This delays start of LSP server until the container is ready.

I would like to convert my plugin configuration to the new LSP config but I am not sure if it is possible to do without the `on_new_config` handler (specifically the part where we wait with LSP start until devcontainer is running).

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> The most important "feature" of `on_new_config` is that it is running in a Lua coroutine.

Should we change any of the existing callbacks to be coroutines?

Why do we need both `before_init` and `on_new_config`? We could drop `before_init` and add `on_config`, just before https://github.com/neovim/neovim/blob/ce097c5091eab3550e1534fd111752577b5813ea/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua#L271
there literally seems to be no reason to have a separate `before_init` if we have `on_config`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> Should we change any of the existing callbacks to be coroutines?

No. If any function needs to be async, then give it a callback argument. We've already done this for `root_dir`.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
Instead of `on_config` and instead of adding some function argument to `vim.tbl_deep_extend`. Could we instead allow the whole configs to be passed as functions with callbacks.

```diff
diff --git a/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua b/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua
index 544466a9fc..de1bac26f1 100644
--- a/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua
+++ b/runtime/lua/vim/lsp.lua
@@ -358,7 +358,7 @@ end
 ---@since 13
 ---
 --- @param name string
---- @param cfg vim.lsp.Config
+--- @param cfg vim.lsp.Config|fun(config: vim.lsp.Config, callback: fun(config: vim.lsp.Config))
 --- @participant14 disable-next-line:assign-type-mismatch
 function lsp.config(name, cfg)
   local _, _ = name, cfg -- ignore unused
```

And do the same for `lsp/*`.

This would also resolve #33615 where some servers require dynamic commands.

The downside of this is that we'd never be able to save resolved configs as they are dynamic and thus `local cfg = vim.lsp.confg('foo')` will incur a much larger perf hit. Though might not be a problem in practice.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> downside of this is that we'd never be able to save resolved configs as they are dynamic

Yeah, also removes opportunity for serialization, auto-generated UIs, and makes troubleshooting harder. But that cost applies to all of these callback approaches.

`on_config:fun()` essentially is equivalent to "undefined behavior". Your proposal isn't any worse than that... so +1 :)

btw, with your proposal, we could also remove `before_init`? It seems to have a very narrow use-case.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
> btw, with your proposal, we could also remove before_init? It seems to have a very narrow use-case.

Yeah, we've never used `before_init` internally. For reference, it was added in #11430, so is a long hang over.

comments.author: participant8
comments.body: @participant1 sorry I'm having some trouble understanding `fun(config: vim.lsp.Config, callback: fun(config: vim.lsp.Config))` in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/issues/32287#issuecomment-2835155023. Could you explain what the parameters correspond to?

comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
`config` is the current value of the config as it is being accumulated. The callback must be called instead of returning the config.

```lua
return function(config, callback)
  config.field = ...
  callback(config)
end)
```

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
In a semi-similar vein as @participant7 above, prior to Neovim 0.11 using `lspconfig`, I ran my language servers using `systemd-run -- <server> [args]`.

https://github.com/participant9/dotfiles/blob/6fe98e2228454972a5f5d9f590e8ff5bf4ffa117/neovim/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/lspconfig/init.lua#L18-L54

https://github.com/participant9/dotfiles/blob/6fe98e2228454972a5f5d9f590e8ff5bf4ffa117/neovim/.config/nvim/lua/plugins/lspconfig/init.lua#L94-L98

https://github.com/participant9/dotfiles/blob/6fe98e2228454972a5f5d9f590e8ff5bf4ffa117/neovim/.config/nvim/lua/participant9/utils/systemd.lua#L3-L65

In Neovim 0.11, I can't seem to _easily_ do that. The benefit of the `lspconfig` approach was that I never had to be aware of the language server's command. I could just do it for all language servers, by just extending their commands. This is great for lazy people, like me. With the current way to configure language servers, I'm left with just copy/pasting the `cmd` field from all the configs. It doesn't help that the programmatic API for `lspconfig` is deprecated, which I think is for the best anyway.

For those who might be wondering why I would wrap language server commands using `systemd-run`, this has the benefit of viewing language server logs through `journalctl(1)` if Neovim ever gains the ability to allow users to configure where the logs go, and not to `vim.fn.stdpath("state")/lsp.log`.

I believe my use case would be covered by the proposal using the following code:

```lua
vim.lsp.config("*", function(config, callback)
  config.cmd = wrap_in_systemd_run(config.cmd)
  callback(config)
end)
```

I thought I would log my use case to help design considerations for when/if the proposal makes it to a release.

comments.body:
@participant10 While not exactly the same, I use `on_init` for this:

```lua
on_init = function(client)
	local ok, workspace_folder = pcall(unpack, client.workspace_folders)
	if not ok then
		return
	end
	local path = workspace_folder.name
	if
		vim.uv.fs_stat(vim.fs.joinpath(path, ".luarc.json"))
		or vim.uv.fs_stat(vim.fs.joinpath(path, ".luarc.jsonc"))
	then
		return
	end

	client.config.settings.Lua =
		---@participant14 disable-next-line: param-type-mismatch
		vim.tbl_deep_extend("force", client.config.settings.Lua, {
			runtime = { version = "LuaJIT" },
			workspace = {
				checkThirdParty = "Disable",
				library = {
					"${3rd}/luv/library",
					unpack(vim.api.nvim_get_runtime_file("", true)),
				},
			},
		})
end,
```

comments.body:
Sorry @participant10 but your use case won't impact the decision here. You need to provide configuration files for the servers you use if they have them. We do not plan to implement a whole mechanism at the editor level to workaround users not wanting to create server specific configuration files.

Any servers that don't have configuration files but define LSP settings should be lobbied to add them.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: With https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34550, if `cmd` is defined as a function it now receives the resolved `config` as the 2nd arg.

comments.author: participant7
comments.body:
After https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34550 I was able to adapt [devcontainers.nvim](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim) to the new `vim.lsp.config` API.

What I needed was to:
1. Find root_dir dynamically
2. Delay startup of LSP server until devcontainer is up (could take very long when `devcontainer up` builds the container)

Solution to 1. is directly provided by https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34550 - just take `config.root_dir` inside `cmd` function.

To solve 2. I made a stub RPC client that queues all requests/notifications until it is resolved - for me it was after `devcontainer up` finished - then it sends them all to LSP server and replaces itself with the actual RPC client. This approach seems to work well - the LSP client is not registered as attached until the "initialize" request is resolved, so user won't be able to use LSP until it's actually ready. The implementation can be found in [devcontainers.lsp.rpc.make_stub](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim/blob/e8e1446d38edfedbb226a18f265eaee92b106388/lua/devcontainers/lsp/rpc.lua#L245) if someone needs it (and [here](https://github.com/participant7/devcontainers.nvim/blob/e8e1446d38edfedbb226a18f265eaee92b106388/lua/devcontainers/init.lua#L152) is the delayed resolve called from coroutine).

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
`on_new_config` has been convenient for me in these use cases:
1. Switch _both_ `config.settings` and `config.cmd` based on `root_dir`. I have a bunch of Bazel projects that use conventional LSPs, but with very specific configuration, while also having projects using the same LSPs with default configuration. So the logic would roughly go like this:
   ```lua
   on_new_config = function(cfg, root_dir)
     if is_bazel_root_dir(root_dir) then
       set_bazel_cfg(cfg)     
     else
       set_default_cfg(cfg)
     end
   end 
   ```
   I acknowledge that this can be achieved with the current API, but e.g. `is_bazel_root_dir` would have to be run twice in some cases (in the functional `cmd` and e.g., in `on_init`), so it's currently much less ergonomic for this "switch" logic.

   I suppose, another way of going about this would be to define two different configs, e.g., `clangd` and `clangd_bazel` and use a functional `root_dir` in both to switch between them based on the project path, but again, that'd just be much more code than currently to no particular benefit.

2. Send file-specific `settings` to the LSP for the same `root_dir`.

   This has been helpful when working in a monorepo where `root_dir` needs to be the root of the repo, but the LSP still requires some package-specific config. Since`on_new_config` is executed for every opened file (unlike `on_init`), one could have something like this:
   ```lua
   on_new_config = function(cfg, root_dir)
     local package = get_package(vim.fn.bufname())
     local package_cfg = set_bazel_cfg(cfg)     
     set_package_cfg(cfg, package_cfg)
   end 
   ```
   
   With the new API, I now have to manually send `workspace/didChangeConfiguration` in a custom autocommand.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
> 1. Switch _both_ `config.settings` and `config.cmd` based on `root_dir`

Did you review the discussion above? `cmd()` function can set `config.settings` and `reuse_client` can decide when to re-invoke `cmd()`.

> 2\. Send file-specific `settings` to the LSP for the same `root_dir`

You can define a `reuse_client` handler which starts a new client for those cases.

comments.author: participant13
comments.body:
> Did you review the discussion above? cmd() function can set config.settings and reuse_client can decide when to re-invoke cmd().
>You can define a reuse_client handler which starts a new client for those cases.

Thanks! Yes, I did, as I've mentioned, I see that it's doable, but it just seems like more work to handle these cases now with the new API. The separation of concerns also seems to be all over the place - using `cmd` for setting the client config seems surprising 🤔 Same with `reuse_client`. There's now much more low-level skill required from the user to set something like this up.

The problem here is essentially that the config is dynamic per `root_dir`, and maybe per buffer.
